<STRUCT_0001>
Flatness is one of the most important technical tools in algebraic geometry.
In this section we introduce this notion. We intentionally limit the discussion
to straightforward observations, apart from Lemma <REF_0001>.
A very important class of results, namely criteria for flatness, are
discussed in
Algebra, Sections <REF_0002>,
<REF_0003>,
<REF_0004>, and
More on Morphisms, Section
<REF_0005>.
There is a chapter dedicated to advanced material on flat morphisms of
schemes, namely More on Flatness, Section <REF_0006>.

<STRUCT_0002><STRUCT_0003>
Recall that a module <MATH_0001> over a ring <MATH_0002> is <TEXTITOPEN_0001>flat<TEXTITCLOSE_0001> if the functor
<MATH_0003> is exact. A ring map
<MATH_0004> is said to be <TEXTITOPEN_0002>flat<TEXTITCLOSE_0002> if <MATH_0005> is flat as an <MATH_0006>-module.
See
Algebra, Definition <REF_0007>.

Let <MATH_0001> be a morphism of schemes.
Let <MATH_0002> be a quasi-coherent sheaf of <MATH_0003>-modules.
<STRUCT_0001>
<STRUCT_0002> We say <MATH_0004> is <TEXTITOPEN_0001>flat at a point <MATH_0005><TEXTITCLOSE_0001> if the
local ring <MATH_0006> is flat over the local ring
<MATH_0007>.
<STRUCT_0003> We say that <MATH_0008> is <TEXTITOPEN_0002>flat over <MATH_0009> at a point <MATH_0010><TEXTITCLOSE_0002>
if the stalk <MATH_0011> is a flat <MATH_0012>-module.
<STRUCT_0004> We say <MATH_0013> is <TEXTITOPEN_0003>flat<TEXTITCLOSE_0003> if <MATH_0014> is flat at every point of <MATH_0015>.
<STRUCT_0005> We say that <MATH_0016> is <TEXTITOPEN_0004>flat over <MATH_0017><TEXTITCLOSE_0004> if
<MATH_0018> is flat over <MATH_0019> at every point <MATH_0020> of <MATH_0021>.
